`{ value }` does not mean a multiplier and must carry a unit. css keeps multipliers and absolute units; sketch's final `lineheight` rounds up to an integer regardless of multiplier, `px`, `pt`, or `rem`. `fontsize`, absolute `lineheight`, and `letterspacing` use a rem base of 16 by default, overridable via `theme.font.$extensions.typography.basefontsize`. wave never converts between px and pt. ### sketch color output in sketch output, every color asset's `color` field is an `#rrggbbaa` hex8 snapshot; colors with alpha or opacity overrides fold transparency into the snapshot's alpha channel. color positions inside layer assets (`shadows[].color`, `gradient.color`) are hex8 snapshots too, with no swatch binding: whether a color token registers `$id` or is skipped by `sketch.skip` only affects whether it appears as a color asset in the manifest, never the values at color positions. the gap layer of an outline is fixed to `#ffffffff`. the legacy `@/ ` string references and the trial `{ "$ref": " " }` bindings are no longer emitted; changing colors on the sketch side requires re-importing the payload. ## dashed borders `border` is a standard composite of `color`, `width`, and `style`. `style` accepts a standard stroke style string, an object with `dasharray` and `linecap`, or a reference to a standalone `strokestyle` token: ```yaml antline: $type: border $value: color: "{theme.color.primary}" width: 1 style: dasharray: - value: 4 unit: px - value: 8 unit: px linecap: butt ``` string styles support `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `outset`, and `inset`. an object style must contain both a non-empty `dasharray` and a `linecap`; `linecap` accepts only `round`, `butt`, `square`. `dasharray` members follow the dimension contract and also accept wave dimension shorthands and extended units. odd-length arrays repeat once; every platform outputs the same even-length array. the dtcg schema does not restrict dash member signs or all-zero combinations; when css cannot express a negative or all-zero pattern, it shows the token path, type, and value shape, then fails. css outputs a usable `dashed` shorthand for object styles plus `-dash-array` and `-line-cap` companion variables, e.g. `--border-antline: 1px dashed #1872f0`, `--border-antline-dash-array: 4px 8px`, and `--border-antline-line-cap: butt`. a companion name colliding with a real token key fails the build. sketch output contains only syncable assets; dashed borders produce no sketch record.

title: Extensions and output
description: Reference for `$extensions` fields and the json, jsonc, css, sketch, and md-yml output formats.
searchText: extensions and output reference for `$extensions` fields and the json, jsonc, css, sketch, and md-yml output formats. design token wave token doctor wave token migrate extensions local cli ## output formats | platform | output file | description | | --- | --- | --- | | `json` | `{theme}.json` | flat json | | `jsonc` | `{theme}.jsonc` | jsonc with comments | | `css` | `{theme}.css` | css variables | | `sketch` | `{theme}2sketch.json` | sketch asset manifest (payload v2) | | `md-yml` | `{theme}2md.yml` | yaml token fragment for markdown frontmatter | css output covers the `color`, `state`, `shadow`, `gradient`, `border`, `radius`, and `font` roots. `theme.dimension` is no longer a public output root; the build suggests migration, and full recommendations come from `wave token doctor`. typography tokens emit field variables in css (`-family`, `-size`, `-weight`, `-line-height`, `-letter-spacing`, optionally `-color`) rather than an aggregate shorthand variable, and emit text asset records in sketch. border tokens with `$extensions.platform.sketch.outline` emit the outline value and offset companions in css, and generate a two-layer shadow that simulates the outline in sketch. ### platform output of standard types json and jsonc output flat key/value; dimension and dimension fields inside composites keep their unit strings. md-yml uses the same final values but groups them by namespace. css emits directly consumable values. sketch output is an asset manifest; only syncable assets produce records: | `$type` | json / jsonc | css | sketch | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `color` | target color space string, or a clean dtcg color object | css color 4 value | `kind: color` record with hex8 color | | `dimension` | `"8px"` | `8px` | `kind: layer` record when in a radius group or generating a sketch property dimension; otherwise no record | | `fontfamily` | string or string array | font stack | no record | | `fontweight` | number | number | no record (text records only accept 100–900 in hundreds) | | `duration` | `"200ms"` | `200ms` | no record | | `cubicbezier` | number array | `cubic-bezier(...)` | no record | | `number` | number | number | `kind: layer` record when in a radius group or generating a sketch property dimension; otherwise no record | | `strokestyle` | string or `{ dasharray, linecap }` | main variable plus dash/line-cap companions | no record | | `border` | `{ color, width, style }` | border shorthand plus required companions | only borders with `platform.sketch.outline` generate a `kind: layer` record | | `transition` | `{ duration, delay, timingfunction }` | transition value | no record | | `shadow` | single-layer object or layer array | box-shadow value | `kind: layer` record (`shadows` field) | | `gradient` | stop array | linear-gradient value | `kind: layer` record (`gradient` field) | | `typography` | five standard fields plus optional wave `color` | field variables | `kind: text` record | when a platform cannot express an input, wave stops the build and reports the token path, type, and reason. typical failures include: a color that css or sketch cannot convert with no `hex` fallback, an empty font family or negative or all-zero dash pattern in css, and relative units sketch native numeric properties cannot represent. for unknown custom `$type`s, css accepts scalars only; objects or arrays fail explicitly, and `[object object]` output is forbidden. when the current directory has a `main.yaml`, `wave token doctor` checks it by default; pass `wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml` to be explicit. multiple platforms are declared in `$config`: ```yaml $config: theme: example parameter: outputdir: ./dist platform: [json, jsonc, css, sketch, md-yml] ``` ## md-yml `md-yml` generates a yaml token fragment that can be copied into markdown frontmatter. with `filterlayer: 1`, the following tokens produce `{theme}2md.yml`: ```yaml color: primary-main: '#1a72f0' primary-on-main: '#ffffff' text-emphasis: '#112233' radius: md: 8px font: font-family: - system-ui - sans-serif heading-h1: color: "{color.text-emphasis}" fontfamily: "{font.font-family}" fontsize: 2.5rem fontweight: 700 letterspacing: 0px lineheight: 1.2 ``` the first output layer is the namespace, and the remaining source path segments join with `-`. so `theme.color.primary.main` becomes `color.primary-main` after filtering `theme`, and document bodies can use: ```markdown {color.primary-main} ``` md-yml keeps theme direct references that project onto the same file and rewrites their paths to output paths. for example, `theme.font.heading.h1` inherits `fontfamily: "{theme.font.font-family}"` from the flat fields of `theme.font.$extensions.typography` and outputs as `fontfamily: "{font.font-family}"`. direct references inside complete tokens, composite sub-fields, and array members follow the same rule. a reference survives only when the target is also emitted into the current payload and the consumer slot is not rewritten by computation. external resource references, `$ref` + override, `smoothshadow` / `smoothgradient`, `inheritcolor` / `currentcolor`, and other computed values still output the final value after resolver and transformer processing. objects, arrays, and explicit composites keep their structure. the file contains no `---` delimiter, `$description` comments, token wrappers, or `$type` / `$value` metadata. after `filterlayer` processing, at least a namespace and a local key must remain. source segments in the path cannot be empty or contain `.`; when different source paths project onto the same key, the build fails. the build also fails before writing any product of that pass when a value contains data yaml cannot represent losslessly, such as `undefined`, non-finite numbers, sparse arrays, or cycles. ## $extensions `$extensions` expresses wave's extension semantics. after the build, extension fields are consumed and never appear verbatim in output files. profiles inherit base tokens and the extensions of existing groups; re-declaring or overriding them is not allowed. `$override` replaces `$value` only and cannot change extension settings like `smoothshadow.target`, `platform.sketch.path`, or `inheritcolor.property.opacity`. when those differences are needed, create a separate base directory; new tokens can declare their own extensions. full boundaries: [profiles and night](/design-token/quality-theming). supported fields: | field | location | applicable types | purpose | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `typography` | group | effective type `typography` | font default fields and rem base; see [colors and typography](/design-token/color-typography) | | `smoothshadow` | token | `shadow` | derive a multi-layer smooth shadow from a single layer | | `smoothgradient` | token | `gradient` | derive a smooth gradient from 2 stops | | `inheritcolor` | token | `color` | emit a context-inheriting color | | `platform.sketch.path` | group or token | any token | adjust the grouping prefix of sketch asset names | | `platform.sketch.skip` | group or token | any token | skip sketch output only | | `platform.sketch.property.opacity` | token | `number` under `theme.state.*` | emit the sketch opacity field | | `platform.sketch.property.cornerradius` | token | radius/dimension tokens | emit the sketch corners.radii field | | `platform.sketch.outline` | border token | `border` | emit a css outline and the sketch two-layer shadow simulation | | `composite` | group | direct children must be tokens | merge a group of tokens into a component object | | `currentcolor` | token | legacy | legacy compatibility field; new content uses `inheritcolor` | the legacy forms `$extensions.sketch.*` and `$extensions.outline` are rejected outright by the build, which points to the migration command. one run in the project directory completes the rename (preview only by default; add `--write` to write back): ```bash wave token migrate extensions --write ``` ## smoothshadow `smoothshadow` applies to `shadow` tokens, deriving a multi-layer smooth shadow from a single layer. ```yaml theme: shadow: $type: shadow card: $value: color: "#00000033" offsetx: 0 offsety: 8 blur: 24 spread: 0 $extensions: smoothshadow: cubicbezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1] step: 4 ``` fields: | field | description | | --- | --- | | `cubicbezier` | 4 numbers, or a curve referenced from a dimension resource | | `step` | number of visible output layers, integer `>= 1` | | `target` | optional target shadow layer; when present, interpolates from the current shadow to the target | the input value must be a single shadow layer object, not an array. with `target`, `step` must be `>= 2`. `target` accepts the same fields as a shadow layer, and can specify the target transparency alone through `alpha`: ```yaml $extensions: smoothshadow: cubicbezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1] step: 4 target: alpha: 0.08 offsetx: 0 offsety: 16 blur: 48 spread: -4 ``` ## smoothgradient `smoothgradient` applies to `gradient` tokens, expanding 2 endpoints into multiple gradient stops. ```yaml theme: gradient: $type: gradient overlay: $value: - color: "#00000000" position: 0 - color: "#000000cc" position: 1 $extensions: smoothgradient: cubicbezier: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1] step: 7 ``` fields: | field | description | | --- | --- | | `cubicbezier` | 4 numbers, or a curve referenced from a dimension resource | | `step` | total stop count, integer `>= 2` | the input gradient must have exactly 2 stops. ## inheritcolor `inheritcolor` applies to `color` tokens, meaning the output inherits the context color. ```yaml theme: color: $type: color icon: $value: "#000000" $extensions: inheritcolor: true iconsubtle: $value: "#000000" $extensions: inheritcolor: property: opacity: 0.36 siblingslot: foreground ``` fields: | field | description | | --- | --- | | `inheritcolor: true` | emit an inheriting color | | `property.opacity` | emit opacity; supports numbers, aliases, `$ref` | | `property.alpha` | emit alpha; supports numbers, aliases, `$ref` | | `siblingslot` | in sketch output, find the sibling color value within the same composite | output differences: | platform | output | | --- | --- | | `css` | `currentcolor` or `color-mix(in srgb, currentcolor x%, transparent)` | | `json` / `jsonc` / `md-yml` | `$color_foreground` or `{ color: "$color_foreground", opacity: x }` | | `sketch` | writes sketch color, `opacity`, or `alpha` fields | ## platform.sketch `$extensions.platform.sketch` only controls sketch json output and does not affect the keys of `json`, `jsonc`, `css`, or `md-yml`. `path` and `skip` can be written on a group or a token; on a group, they apply to descendant tokens. ```yaml theme: color: $type: color $extensions: platform: sketch: path: foundation/color primary: $value: "#1872f0" state: hover: $type: number $value: 0.16 $extensions: platform: sketch: path: foundation/interaction property: opacity: true radius: card: $type: dimension $value: "12px" $extensions: platform: sketch: property: cornerradius: true ``` fields: | field | description | | --- | --- | | `platform.sketch.path` | slash grouping prefix of sketch asset names, e.g. `foundation/color`; can be written on a group or a token | | `platform.sketch.skip` | when `true`, omits sketch output; a descendant group or token may explicitly write `false` to restore output | | `platform.sketch.property.opacity` | writes the `opacity` number in layer records | | `platform.sketch.property.cornerradius` | writes the `corners.radii` number in layer records | | `platform.sketch.outline` | border tokens only; generates the two-layer shadow outline simulation per `offset` and makes css emit outline variables | `path` uses slash grouping as the prefix of asset names. assuming `filterlayer: 1`, the color token above produces an asset named `foundation/color/primary`; without `path`, the name is the leaf key after `filterlayer` processing. priority: 1. the token's own `path` 2. the nearest parent group's `path` 3. the `path` of a higher ancestor group `property` does not inherit. to emit `opacity` or `corners.radii`, it must still be written on the corresponding token. `skip` accepts booleans only, inherits from the nearest declaration, and the token's own value wins. an explicit `false` overrides an ancestor group's `true`. this switch filters sketch output only; css, json, jsonc, and md-yml still emit the token. limits: - `path` must be a plain slash grouping path, e.g. `foundation/color`; leading/trailing slashes, empty segments, and `.` are not allowed. - `property` supports only `opacity` and `cornerradius`, the value must be `true`, and it can only be written on tokens. - `property.opacity` applies to `number` tokens under `theme.state.*`. - `property.cornerradius` applies to radius/dimension tokens under `theme.radius.*` or `theme.dimension.*`. - `outline` takes effect only on border tokens. - unknown fields, unknown properties, or misplaced usage fail the build. for example, `$type: number` with `property.fillcolor: true` errors because `fillcolor` is not a supported sketch property; `$type: color` with `property.opacity: true` errors because `opacity` only accepts state number tokens. - unknown platforms under `platform.*` (e.g. `platform.figma`) only produce warnings and do not affect the build; they are reserved compatibility slots for future platforms. ## sketch asset manifest the `sketch` platform outputs a json asset manifest: the root holds `meta` and `assets`, with one asset per line inside `assets` for easy human review and git diff. ```json { "meta": { "themeid": "6f1c2a54b7d84e0f9a1c32d45e6b70f8", "baseid": null, "version": 2 }, "assets": [ { "uuid": "0f8e6d5c4b3a29180f7e6d5c4b3a2918", "name": "foundation/color/primary-main", "kind": "color", "color": "#1872f0ff" }, { "name": "foundation/interaction/hover", "kind": "layer", "opacity": 0.16 } ] } ``` - `meta.themeid` comes from the current day document's root `$id`: main output uses main's identity, named profile output uses that profile's own identity; `null` when missing. use `wave token ids --write` to fill in document identity. night inherits the corresponding day's identity. - `meta.baseid` is the main's root `$id` in named profile (including its night) output, and `null` in main (including its night) output. it is a payload v2 addition, and `version` stays fixed at `2`; if the sketch plugin strictly validates the legacy `meta` field set, confirm the plugin accepts `baseid` first — do not judge compatibility by the version number alone. - every record carries `name` and `kind`; when the token has a registered token-level `$id`, it also carries `uuid`, otherwise that field is omitted. - `kind` has exactly three values: `color` (color tokens, corresponding to swatches), `text` (typography tokens, corresponding to shared text styles), and `layer` (shadows, gradients, outline borders, corner dimensions, etc., corresponding to shared layer styles). - only syncable assets enter the manifest: plain borders, plain dimensions, transitions, and the like produce no records. - text records contain only font fields (`fontfamily`, `fontsize`, `fontweight`, `lineheight`, `kerning`), never the text color; `fontweight` accepts only the 100–900 hundreds scale, and other values error immediately at sketch build time, leaving css and json unaffected. - layer records combine fields such as `shadows`, `gradient`, `opacity`, and `corners`; `fills` and `gradient` are mutually exclusive within one record. - records follow the token order in the theme files; renaming or changing anything besides `path` does not disturb the order. asset names must be unique within one manifest: when two tokens produce exactly the same name, the build errors. slashes in names are plain characters, and overlapping prefixes are not conflicts — `shadow` and `shadow/elevation-1` can coexist. color positions in layer records always carry `#rrggbbaa` hex8 color snapshots with no swatch binding; color assets in the same manifest still carry `uuid` by their own `$id` for sync token adoption. details: [colors and typography](/design-token/color-typography). ## composite `composite` merges a group's direct child tokens into one component object. suited to component variants such as buttons and cards. ```yaml component: button: outline: $extensions: composite: true fill: $value: "{theme.color.surface}" border: $value: "{theme.color.primary}" radius: $value: "9999px" ``` rules: - `composite` is written on the group's `$extensions`. - direct children of a composite group must all be tokens; further group nesting is not allowed. - json/jsonc/md-yml output merges into an object. - sketch output no longer maps composites to component style fields; component logic will be designed separately later.

title: Profile and Night model
description: Understand identity, overrides, and directory relationships of base, Day profiles, and Night overlays.
searchText: profile and night model understand identity, overrides, and directory relationships of base, day profiles, and night overlays. design token wave token local cli ## base and profiles `main.yaml` is the base and the project baseline. one base together with its day profiles forms a series; different structures should use separate base workspaces. a profile uses a closed `$config`: ```yaml $id: dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd $config: base: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa $override: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb: $value: "#1872f0" theme: color: accent: $type: color $value: "#ff3366" ``` - `$config.base` must equal the main's registered root `$id` verbatim. - `$override` keys are base token `$id`s, not token paths or document ids. - each entry contains only `$value`; objects and arrays are replaced wholesale, with no sub-field merging. - new tokens must not collide with existing paths; existing groups must not re-declare metadata. - new token types must be determinable from the profile itself. - a profile cannot delete base tokens, change existing types, or modify existing extensions. reference expressions survive profile merging until the reference resolution stage; they are not materialized in advance. ## directories and base location explicit `-f` does not depend on fixed directory names: ```text main.yaml profiles/mobile.yaml themes/mobile.yaml variants/mobile.yaml ``` all of these day profiles are valid. wave walks up from the profile's directory to the nearest `main.yaml`, then verifies `$config.base`. `--profiles all` still uses the existing workspace discovery rules and does not recursively guess yaml in arbitrary directories. the legacy variant model and `--variant` parameter are unsupported, but `variants/` works as an ordinary directory name. ## night is a path override night is an override file for day, not a profile, and does not use `$override`: ```yaml theme: color: primary: $value: "#93c5fd" ``` night only overrides leaves that day already has under `theme.color` and `theme.state`; a root `$id` is forbidden, and day document and token identity carry over. default file relationship: ```text main.yaml → main@night.yaml themes/mobile.yaml → themes/mobile@night.yaml variants/mobile.yaml → variants/mobile@night.yaml ``` select the original day source document explicitly at build time: ```bash wave token build -f ./main.yaml --night wave token build -f ./themes/mobile.yaml --night ``` a missing or generally invalid overlay warns and is skipped; identity violations fail. ## related tasks - create a profile: [create a workspace and profiles](/design-token/create) - create an overlay: [create a night overlay](/design-token/night) - check structure: [check a token workspace](/design-token/doctor) - check contrast: [check wcag contrast](/design-token/wcag) - maintain identity: [maintain token identity](/design-token/ids)

title: Asset compression
description: Compress PNG, JPG, SVG, and GIF assets, and control preview, output, and writing.
searchText: asset compression compress png, jpg, svg, and gif assets, and control preview, output, and writing. assets wave compress wave compress doctor wave compress install local cli ## preview compression ```bash wave compress -f ./assets --dry-run ``` the input can be a file or a directory; the default is the current directory. `--dry-run` shows the real compression results without writing files. ## write output ```bash wave compress -f ./assets --yes wave compress -f ./assets --output ./optimized --yes ``` by default, output goes to `wave-compress/` under the input directory; source files are never overwritten. `--yes` only skips the confirmation; overwriting existing output still requires `--force`. ## scope and quality ```bash wave compress -f ./assets --type png --type jpg --recursive wave compress -f ./assets --type png --quality 80 ``` `--type` only accepts repeated flags, not comma-joined values. supported types: `png`, `jpg`, `svg`, `gif`. without `--quality`, the default safe policy applies. passing a value from 1–100 enables lossy quality mode. ## svg icon cleanup ```bash wave compress -f ./assets --type svg --icon --yes ``` `--icon` cleans svg icon colors so they can be recolored through css. ## toolchain ```bash wave compress doctor wave compress install --check wave compress install --yes ``` check the tools first, review the install plan, then confirm the installation.

title: Motion generation
description: Generate GIF or APNG from a directory of PNG frames, controlling format, output, and overwriting.
searchText: motion generation generate gif or apng from a directory of png frames, controlling format, output, and overwriting. assets wave motion wave motion doctor wave motion install local cli ## generate motion ```bash wave motion -f ./frames --format gif wave motion -f ./frames --format apng ``` the input directory needs at least two png frames. non-interactive environments must pass `--format gif|apng` explicitly; in a tty, omitting the format opens an interactive choice. ## output ```bash wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --output ./loading.gif wave motion -f ./frames --format apng --output ./loading.png ``` by default, output goes to `wave-mg/` under the frames directory; the file name contains the frames directory name and the fps. existing output is rejected by default; confirm first, then use `--force`. preview the plan only: ```bash wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --dry-run ``` ## encoding parameters ```bash wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --fps 24 --quality 80 --loop forever ``` | parameter | default | | --- | --- | | `--fps ` | 24 | | `-q, --quality ` | 80 | | `--loop ` | `forever`; also supports `once` | the command never modifies the source frames. ## toolchain and frame checks ```bash wave motion doctor wave motion doctor -f ./frames wave motion install --check wave motion install --yes ``` `motion doctor` accepts an optional `-f` png frames directory to check the frame input at the same time.

title: Workspace creation
description: Create design project directories from local configuration, controlling target location and existing content.
searchText: workspace creation create design project directories from local configuration, controlling target location and existing content. workspace wave workspace local cli ## create a workspace ```bash wave workspace ``` the command asks for project name, type, version, and tags per the configuration, then creates the directory structure and readme. no `create` subcommand is needed. preview the plan only: ```bash wave workspace --dry-run ``` skip the write confirmation: ```bash wave workspace --yes ``` ## target location ```bash wave workspace --output ./my-project --yes ``` `--output` points at the final workspace directory, not a parent. the logical project name still comes from the interactive answers. existing targets are rejected by default. with `--force`, wave only overwrites the readme and placeholder files this run would generate, keeps other files in the directory, and never deletes content recursively. plain files and symlinks as targets are still rejected. ## configuration file default path: ```text ~/.config/wave/workspace.yaml ``` use another configuration: ```bash wave_workspace_config=/path/to/workspace.yaml wave workspace ``` when the file is missing, built-in defaults apply. `wave_workspace_config` affects workspace only, not the token resource cache.

title: Command index
description: Find Wave commands by task and get the Markdown manual at the matching level.
searchText: command index find wave commands by task and get the markdown manual at the matching level. reference wave local cli ## common commands ```bash wave token wave compress -f ./assets --dry-run wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --dry-run wave workspace --dry-run ``` `wave token` builds the current directory's `main.yaml` by default. compression, motion, and workspace commands also run their tasks directly, with no extra `run`, `gif`, or `create` subcommand. ## design token | command | purpose | | --- | --- | | `wave token build` | generate token outputs | | `wave token new` | create a token workspace | | `wave token new profile ` | create a profile from a registered base | | `wave token new night` | create a night overlay from a day main or profile | | `wave token doctor` | check workspace, resources, and identity | | `wave token wcag` | check color contrast | | `wave token ids` | report or write back document and token identity | | `wave token migrate extensions` | migrate legacy `$extensions` syntax | | `wave token show` | browse built-in resources | | `wave token update [name]` | update the resource cache | | `wave token status` | show resource cache status | the bare `wave token` command equals `wave token build`. `migrate` has no default migration target; `extensions` must be written explicitly. ## asset toolchain ```bash wave compress doctor wave compress install --check wave motion doctor -f ./frames wave motion install --check ``` `--check` only shows the install plan. add `--yes` only after confirming. ## global commands | command | purpose | | --- | --- | | `wave doctor` | check the local runtime and toolchain | | `wave install` | review or run recommended tool installation | | `wave workspace` | create a design project workspace | | `wave manual` | launch the visual web manual | | `wave version` | show the version | ## get the manual `--help` gives concise help. `-m, --manual` prints structured markdown for the current command scope, suited for agents: ```bash wave -m wave token -m wave token new -m wave token new night -m wave token migrate extensions -m ``` documentation mode runs no builds, creation, compression, or encoding, and never starts a web server.

title: Configuration paths
description: Locate Wave's workspace configuration, resource cache, and default output locations.
searchText: configuration paths locate wave's workspace configuration, resource cache, and default output locations. reference wave token status wave workspace --help local cli ## workspace configuration ```text ~/.config/wave/workspace.yaml ``` override the path: ```bash wave_workspace_config=/path/to/workspace.yaml wave workspace ``` ## resource cache ```bash wave token status ``` output includes cache, state, and config paths, plus the tailwind css and leonardo cache state. ## token output configured in `main.yaml`: ```yaml $config: theme: example parameter: outputdir: ./dist platform: [json, css] ``` command-line override of the output directory for one run: ```bash wave token build -f ./main.yaml --output ./dist ``` the platform list is maintained only in `$config`; there is no cli `--platform`. ## profile and night output default locations: ```text profiles/ .yaml / @night.yaml ``` both accept `--output` for a custom file. custom locations do not widen implicit discovery; see the corresponding creation manuals for how they are consumed later. ## compress output ```text /wave-compress/ ``` override the output directory: ```bash wave compress -f ./assets --output ./optimized --yes ``` ## motion output ```text /wave-mg/ @ fps.gif /wave-mg/ @ fps.png ``` use `--output` to specify the complete output file path.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Use the right check entry points to locate environment, source document, write, and toolchain issues.
searchText: troubleshooting use the right check entry points to locate environment, source document, write, and toolchain issues. reference wave doctor wave token doctor wave token wcag wave compress doctor wave motion doctor local cli ## where to start ```bash wave --help wave -m wave doctor --status ``` `--help` shows concise command help, `-m` prints the markdown manual for the current scope, and `doctor` checks the local toolchain. ## main.yaml not found `wave token` reads the current directory's `main.yaml` by default. for a new project, run first: ```bash wave token new wave token ``` for an existing project, use `-f`: ```bash wave token build -f /path/to/main.yaml wave token build -f /path/to/workspace-directory ``` ## main.yaml missing $config the entry document must contain a valid `$config`: ```yaml $config: theme: example parameter: outputdir: ./dist platform: [json, css] ``` use `wave token doctor -f ./main.yaml` to check structure and resources. ## profile fails to build ```bash wave token doctor -f /path/to/profile.yaml wave token ids -f /path/to/main.yaml ``` check: - the profile sits in the base main's directory or a subdirectory of it. - `$config.base` equals the main's original root `$id`. - `$override` uses registered token `$id`s. - new token types can be determined from the profile itself. to create a profile, register the base first, then run `wave token new profile -f ./main.yaml`. ## night is not built confirm the overlay sits next to the day source document and is named ` @night.yaml`. then select the original day source explicitly: ```bash wave token build -f /path/to/day-or-profile.yaml --night ``` custom `--output` locations are not auto-discovered. profile night cannot be consumed by building main alone. ## output already exists new source documents and motion output never overwrite existing targets by default. preview the plan with `--dry-run` first, then add `--force` after confirming the overwrite: ```bash wave token new night -f ./main.yaml --force wave motion -f ./frames --format gif --force ``` `--yes` only skips the confirmation; it does not grant overwrite permission. ## missing tools ```bash wave compress doctor wave compress install --check wave motion doctor wave motion install --check ``` run the matching `install --yes` only after confirming the install plan. ## command does not exist the only token entry today is `wave token`; motion has no `mg`. common migrations: | old form | current form | | --- | --- | | `wave dt build` | `wave token build` | | `wave dt init` | `wave token new` | | `wave night` | `wave token new night` | | `wave compress run` | `wave compress` | | `wave motion gif` | `wave motion --format gif` | | `wave workspace create` | `wave workspace` | | `--out` | `--output` |
